solver_under_test.objective: MAXIMISE sum of weights over a vertex-disjoint set of EXACTLY k edges
return_semantics: first element = tuple of INPUT EDGE INDICES (not pairs)
infeasible -> (None, None, nodes, False): failed stays False
node-limit -> (None, None, nodes, True): failed=True, value None
returned optimum is the lexicographically smallest optimum under canonical (u,v) key u<=v (pass 2, source L96-130)
solver_under_test.signature_from_source: solve_exact_k(edges: Sequence[Tuple[str,str]], weights: Sequence[float], k: int) -> (edge_indices|None, value|None, nodes: int, failed: bool)

v1_random_graphs.infeasible_reporting_note: solver reports infeasible as (None, None, failed=False); failed=True is reserved for node-limit breaches
v1_random_graphs.k_selection: sorted set {0, 1, max_matching, max_matching+1, n_edges+1, random(0..max_matching+1)}

v4_dense_timing.selection: GLOBAL top-50 by n_edges over all 500 groups (data/states.jsonl main batch 40012-40500 + unmerged seed_40001..40011 shards), plus 3 explicit zero-edge day-0 states; k = k_greedy from the state record; weights = P_hat (frozen artifact); one timed solve per state, no warm-up special-casing (battery already warm)

supplemental_val_top50.note: diagnostic only, NOT part of the gate: top-50 within val groups 40401-40500 (the alternative selection the brief allows)

v5_small_states_bruteforce.brute_force: exhaustive enumeration of ALL size-k index subsets (itertools.combinations + disjoint filter)
v5_small_states_bruteforce.source: pilot seed 40001 match states with n_edges <= 14
